s2: Here is a home in Meyerland. Flood zone A E, and this spot flooded in Harvey. Next to it: flood history at the nearest gauge, evacuation zone and storm surge, Harvey high-water marks, and flood insurance claims for the ZIP code. On the right, live National Weather Service alerts, the rainfall outlook, and nearby river gauges. Every fact links to its source.
s3: Now a drive along Allen Parkway, during a clearly labelled simulated storm. Avoid this route. It names the exact flood-prone crossings out of 128 we mapped, adds community reports and weather warnings, and it never calls a road safe.
s6: After a flood, it walks you through FEMA aid, insurance deadlines, appeals, scam warnings, and safety. It also works offline, by S M S, and with push alerts for your saved places.
s4: Ask a question in Spanish, and our Gemini agent answers in Spanish, with cited sources, and a trace showing how it answered. You can also just talk to it, with Gemini Live voice and ElevenLabs speech, in five languages. Not official guidance. In an emergency, call 911.
s5: Everything is measured on the judge page. A strict audit shows FloodReady reduces harm for 33 of 52 Houston flood problems, with 243 tests passing, and it works even without any API keys. The next storm will come. Your answer should be ready.
